newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard d'Estaing says dlr-Ffr level appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Giscard d'Estaing says dlr-Ffr level appropriate.

text.p: Former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said the dollar-franc level was now "appropriate," the newspaper the International Herald Tribune reported on Thursday.

"We are in a very good target zone," he was quoted as saying. Giscard d'Estaing touched off controvery late last year when he called for a "lower level" for the franc against dollar. When he made the call, the dollar was worth about five francs.
He also said there was "no reason for French interest rates at present to be higher than German rates. I think French interest rates can, and should be, reduced to the same range."
The dollar-franc level stood at 5.6750 to the dollar at 0821 GMT.

Giscard d'Estaing said he told French president Jacques Chirac last summer about his call for a lower franc, and "he said I was right about the idea for a stronger dollar, but he thought it would be very difficult."
Giscard d'Estaing said, however, he did not submit his statement for Chirac's approval but acted on his own behalf "and tried to avoid any contradictions with French policy."
